new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (48 pp., text layer; the PDF's metadata gives the title 'Li: Sortal classifiers and noun categorization in Zauzou', Language and Linguistics 25:2 (2024) pp. 270-317, DOI 10.1075/lali.00155.li, CC BY 4.0). extracted text of PDF page 2 = printed p. 271, section '1. Introduction: Language overview', second paragraph, reads exactly: 'Zauzou is an isolating and tonal language. The basic word order is SOV.' -- verbatim match. Identity: the same page opens 'Zauzou [zɔ⁵⁵zo³³, ISO 639-3 code zal] is a threatened Lolo-Burmese language spoken in Yunnan province', Tu'e Township, Lanping County, Jiangmo dialect, ~3,300 speakers, citing Sun et al. 2002, Chen 2019, Li 2020, Miyagishi 2022 -- this is…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No source opened says where word stress falls. The primary describers state only that Zauzou is a tone language with six lexical tones (55 33 53 31 35 13); every syllable carries a lexically determined tone and tone alternations do morphological work (noun/verb pairs, classifier derivation). Nothing about stress, accent or prominence is stated in any accessible source.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Corroborating tonal statements: Miyagishi 2020, 安田女子大学大学院紀要 25: 21 (file): '声調を持つ点でも，同じく孤立語的である中国語と一致する。' [In having tones, too, it agrees with Chinese, likewise an isolating language]; fn. 1: '声調の表記は数字で示し，13は低中, 31は中低. 33は中中. 35は中高. 53は高中. 55は高高を表す。' [Tones are written with numerals: 13 low-mid, 31 mid-low, 33 mid-mid, 35 mid-high, 53 high-mid, 55 high-high]. Handel 2003 reports that Sun et al. 2002 leave tone sandhi undescribed.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone; Li's and Miyagishi's data are the Jiangmo (江末) dialect of Tu'e Township; Sun et al. 2002 describe both Guoli and Jiangmo varieties. Sandhi tones appear in compounds (Handel 2003, fn. 5).
new_statements.identity_note: All modern fieldwork sources (Li Yu 2018-2025; Miyagishi & Li 2018-2022) describe the Jiangmo (江末) dialect of Tu'e Township, Lanping County; Sun et al. 2002 cover both local varieties, Guoli (果力) and Jiangmo, which are mutually intelligible and treated as one language (no separate glottocodes). The Japanese literature calls the language ゾゾ語 (若柔語), the Chinese literature 柔若语; autonym zau55 zou33.
